quai-dorsay-cuba--linea-clasica.description: Created in 1974 by Cubatabaco for the French market at Seita's request, Quai d'Orsay is named after the Paris quay where Seita kept its offices. Every size is long filler with Vuelta Abajo leaf, and a 2017 relaunch added the No. 50 and No. 54 beside the Coronas Claro. It smokes smooth and delicate, with cream, grass and a soft sweetness, for a slow morning cigar.

thirds.notes: Soft cream and a little vanilla open on a very light smoke, with only a faint sweetness behind them.
The cream recedes for grassy notes and a fresh, fruity sweetness while the smoke gains a little density.
Cream comes back with a hint of coffee and a touch of oak, the profile staying gentle to the end.

quai-dorsay-cuba--edicion-limitada.description: Quai d'Orsay entered the Ediciones Limitadas for the first time in 2019 with the Senadores, a 48 x 157 mm cigar in the Hermosos No. 2 format, presented in France in special boxes of 25. Like every Limited Edition it is rolled from leaf aged at least two years; Habanos points to a delicate aroma and hints of sweet pastry.

quai-dorsay-cuba--edicion-regional.description: Much of Quai d'Orsay's newer work has come through Ediciones Regionales, several of them for France. The Belicoso Royal, 52 x 125 mm, marked the brand's 40th year in 2,000 numbered boxes of 25 sold through the Seita network from early 2014, and the Secreto Cubano, 40 x 110 mm, followed for France in 2016. Habanos describes the Belicoso Royal as smooth and subtle, with pastry notes.
